item.title: The Fed Raised Rates. What Comes Next?
item.description: Kevin M. Warsh, the chairman of the Federal Reserve, on Wednesday left open-ended how much more interest rates may have to rise to tame inflation.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith
item.media:description: Kevin M. Warsh exiting after delivering remarks in Washington on Wednesday.

item.title: Who Will Win the Midterms? Republicans Are Reeling.
item.description: The party is putting up a costly defense of states and districts that President Trump won easily in 2024. And in places like Georgia, strategists wonder if it’s too late.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein and Shane Goldmacher
item.media:description: The political environment has worsened for Republicans as they try to defend control of Congress, though the party has a big cash advantage over Democrats.

item.title: Jewish Leaders in Michigan Urge Support for El-Sayed’s Senate Bid
item.description: The public petition comes after other Michigan Jews registered their discontent with Abdul El-Sayed, the state’s Democratic Senate nominee.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:description: The show of support by Jewish voters for Dr. Abdul El-Sayed appears aimed at countering a push from other Jews in Michigan who oppose him or are threatening to.

item.title: Democrats Hope Voting Rights Decision Will Drive Black Turnout in South
item.description: Black Democratic candidates for governor, the Senate and the House are hoping that attacks on Black representation will bring out Black voters in November.
item.dc:creator: Emily Cochrane
item.media:description: “Discussion around voting and access to the right to vote is energizing, period,” said Keisha Lance Bottoms (left) who is running for governor in Georgia as Senator Jon Ossoff (right) runs for re-election.

item.title: Trump’s Minnesota Surge Threatened Democracy, Judge Warns
item.description: In a rare interview, Patrick Schiltz, who served as the federal court’s chief judge last winter, called the administration’s actions “a grave threat to the rule of law.”
item.dc:creator: Mattathias Schwartz
item.media:credit: Jenn Ackerman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz in his courtroom. A former clerk for Justice Antonin Scalia of the Supreme Court, he does not have the profile of a jurist likely to engage in a high-stakes standoff with the executive branch.

item.title: State Department Extends Visa Ban on Abbas, Other Palestinian Officials
item.description: The move would prevent Mahmoud Abbas, the leader of two governing Palestinian groups, from traveling to the United States next week for the United Nations General Assembly.
item.dc:creator: Edward Wong
item.media:description: Mahmoud Abbas, the leader of the Palestine Liberation Organization and the Palestinian Authority, shown in May, has been denied a visa to attend the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

item.title: Park Service Steamrolls Through Review of Trump’s Arch
item.description: Despite objections from preservationists, final approval for the 250-foot-tall monument appears on track for November.
item.dc:creator: Emily Badger
item.media:description: The arch’s proposed location at Memorial Circle would block the view toward Robert E. Lee’s Arlington House, top left.

item.title: House Passes Bill Taking Aim at Data Center Electricity Costs
item.description: The measure would direct state regulators to consider rules requiring data centers to cover higher energy costs, but it would not compel them to do so.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold
item.media:description: In an aerial view, the Stargate Oracle A.I. data center campus in Abilene, Texas in August. Lawmakers in both parties have called on Congress to impose guardrails on artificial intelligence.

item.title: Trump Wanted Canada as the 51st State. He Ended Up Pushing It Toward the European Union.
item.description: The invitation by the E.U. for Canada to become an “associate member” is a sign of Mr. Trump’s brand of diplomacy, which often involves threatening America’s closest friends.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater and Michael Crowley
item.media:description: President Donald J. Trump with Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada in the Oval Office last October.

item.title: Here’s a Guide to the Midterm Sprint
item.description: We break down the state of the race.
item.dc:creator: Jess Bidgood

item.title: Congress Clears Russia Sanctions Bill, Sending It to Trump
item.description: The bipartisan measure targets financing for Russia’s war against Ukraine as attacks intensify. It passed the House over the objections of Democrats who opposed handing President Trump new tariff powers.
item.dc:creator: Robert Jimison
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Oil facilities in Krasnoyarsk, Russia. The bipartisan measure that passed on Wednesday would impose sanctions on Russian officials, oligarchs, financial institutions and energy companies.

item.title: Takeaways From a Wild Primary Season
item.description: A look back at the good, the bad and the bizarre from the battles that helped set the stage for the coming midterms.
item.dc:creator: Tim Balk
item.media:credit: Desiree Rios for The New York Times
item.media:description: A watch party for Attorney General Ken Paxton of Texas, who won a runoff for the state’s Republican nomination for Senate in May.

item.title: U.S. Intelligence Warns of China Theft Over Sale of F-35 Jets to Saudis
item.description: Internal reports, including one from the Pentagon’s Defense Intelligence Agency, say China could acquire U.S. jet technology through spying or cooperation with Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: Edward Wong and Dustin Volz
item.media:description: An F-35 jet seen last year. Saudi Arabia and the United States have a decades-long history of military cooperation, and the kingdom is by far the largest buyer of American weapons and defense equipment.

item.title: Why Israel Wants More One-Ton Bombs From the U.S.
item.description: The Trump administration plans to deliver 60,000 of the powerful munitions at a time when opposition is growing in Washington to arms sales to Israel.
item.dc:creator: David M. Halbfinger and John Ismay
item.media:credit: Samar Abu Elouf for The New York Times
item.media:description: The remains of a building destroyed by an Israeli airstrike in Gaza in 2023.

item.title: Senate Takes Up Bill to Regulate ‘Wild West’ of Collegiate Sports
item.description: Critics argue the legislation would limit the rights of college athletes while maintaining the power and financial gains of schools and coaches.
item.dc:creator: Carl Hulse
item.media:description: In a strong bipartisan vote, senators agreed on Tuesday to open debate on the Protect College Sports Act.

item.title: Susie Wiles, Trump’s Chief of Staff, Says She Is ‘Cancer Free’
item.description: Ms. Wiles, the first woman to be the White House chief of staff, had said in March that she had breast cancer.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.media:credit: Eric Lee for The New York Times
item.media:description: Susie Wiles, the White House chief of staff, has said she is cancer free.

item.title: House Holds Leon Black in Contempt Over Epstein Subpoenas
item.description: The billionaire investor had refused to appear for a deposition and turn over documents to a key panel investigating Jeffrey Epstein.
item.dc:creator: Michael Gold
item.category: House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform
item.media:description: The House Oversight Committee issued subpoenas to Leon Black in June, after he refused to answer questions about nondisclosure agreements that he had signed with women, some of whom had been linked to Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Officer Sues Capitol Police, Alleging Racial Bias
item.description: It was the latest in a string of discrimination complaints against the department, which has paid out nearly $1 million since 2022 for employment claims.
item.dc:creator: Catie Edmondson
item.media:credit: Jason Andrew for The New York Times
item.media:description: Carneysha Mendoza alleged in a complaint that the Capitol Police are “engaged in an effort to reverse diversity, equity and inclusion gains and eliminate diversity in leadership within the department.”

item.title: Trump Ally Harold Hamm Strikes Venezuela Oil Deal
item.description: Mr. Hamm’s company, Continental Resources, has signed a preliminary deal with Venezuela’s state-owned oil company to develop and produce oil.
item.dc:creator: Brad Plumer and Rebecca F. Elliott
item.media:description: Harold Hamm has been a major donor to President Trump’s political campaigns and made his fortune drilling for oil in the United States.

item.title: U.S. Fast-Tracked Deportation of Ecuadorean Politician Despite Torture Fears
item.description: The removal of José Serrano, a critic of President Daniel Noboa who has been accused of criminal activity, underscores how the Trump administration has asserted control over U.S. immigration courts.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Nehamas, José María León Cabrera, Hamed Aleaziz and Genevieve Glatsky
item.media:description: José Serrano in 2018, when he was president of Ecuador’s National Assembly. He is now being held in a maximum-security prison in the country.
